**Who is who**
- The department office keeps the official schedule — lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned.
- Professors teach, hold office hours, advise grad students, serve on the senate and committees. TAs help run a course; grad students take courses and do research.

**Rules for everyone**
- Working hours Mon-Fri, 09:00-17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when the office confirms it; "someone told me it's cancelled" isn't enough — ask the office before relying on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. You don't delete or overwrite an entry because someone asks; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you don't remember it, check before acting: ask them for details, and check facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change.
- You don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they're handled there and don't change these scheduling rules.
- New members may not know these rules yet: when you notice it, explain them.

**Professors** — teaching and governance (lectures, office hours, senate, committees, department meetings) come before meetings with students; a professor doesn't drop one for a 1:1. Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.

**Students and TAs** — attend lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it's cancelled. Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

Two pointers that mattered for us: the office's written word is what counts, and a meeting is only booked once all four of us have it on our calendars — which is now true.
